name: Göteborg Landvetter Airport
before:
Sweden's second largest airport after Stockholm Arlanda, 20 km east south east of Gothenburg and 40 km west of Borås. It carried just over 5.3 million passengers in 2024 and is also a significant freight airport.

Since Göteborg City Airport closed to commercial flights, this is the city's only passenger airport, so there is no alternative to weigh up.

The gate arrangement is worth knowing. The old domestic and international terminals merged into one building in 2014, and the transfer area with its shops and restaurants is open to all passengers. Gates 10 to 19 now handle everything inside the Schengen area, and gates 22 to 24 sit in the international transit area for non-Schengen flights. There are eleven air bridges at gates 12 to 17 and 19 to 23; the rest are bus gates, so not every departure walks onto the aircraft.

The airport is named after Landvetter, the locality it sits in, and is run by Swedavia.
after:
Sweden's second largest airport after Stockholm Arlanda, 20 km east south east of Gothenburg and 40 km west of Borås. It handled about 5.4 million passengers in 2025 and is also an important cargo airport.

Göteborg City Airport no longer takes passenger flights, which leaves Landvetter as the city's only passenger airport. Not every departure boards by air bridge, as some gates are bus gates. The airport is run by Swedavia.
